**Answer: 12**

This rests partly on recalled search results that I did not recompute here.

**Constraints.** Suppose p, p+d, …, p+(k−1)d are all prime with k ≥ 3 and p > k. For any prime q ≤ k, if q did not divide d, then the terms would cover every residue mod q. One of them would then be divisible by q, and it would have to equal q, which is impossible since p > k. So d must be divisible by every prime ≤ k.

- For k = 12, d must be a multiple of 2·3·5·7·11 = 2310.
- For k = 13, d must be a multiple of 30030.

**Length 12 exists below 1,000,000.** From my memory of published lists of minimal prime progressions, the smallest progression of 12 primes starts at 482611 with common difference 30030. Its last term is 482611 + 11·30030 = 812941, which is below 1,000,000. I did not re-verify the primality of each term.

**Length 13 does not fit.** A progression of 13 primes needs d ≥ 30030, so its terms span at least 12·30030 = 360360. The smallest known 13-term progression of primes has a last term well above 1,000,000, in the millions. That is also from memory, and I did not exhaustively check every starting prime and multiple of 30030 below 1,000,000. Longer progressions are larger still, because each additional term needs a larger forced difference.

The largest possible length is therefore 12.

ANSWER: 12
